skill.name: frontend-slides
skill.description: Create zero-dependency, animation-rich HTML slide decks from briefs, content, images, or PowerPoint files.
skill.summary: Build responsive HTML presentations with curated styles, viewport-safe layouts, animations, and optional PPTX conversion.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives from markdown backticks, CSS selectors, and design terminology. Confirmed risks are third-party font loading and explicit command execution for PPTX conversion or opening generated HTML. No prompt injection or data-exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Generated presentations can load fonts from Fontshare.
remediation.suggestion: Make external font loading opt-in, document the network request, or embed approved local font assets when possible.

remediation.issue: PPTX conversion requires running a Python script and may install python-pptx.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running the script or installing packages, and prefer pinned dependencies in a trusted environment.

remediation.issue: The delivery flow can launch generated HTML with the system open command.
remediation.suggestion: Ask before opening generated files and clearly state that the browser will execute the presentation JavaScript.

content.value_statement: Teams need polished presentations that work in a browser without a build step. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to create responsive HTML decks with curated styles, animations, and PPTX conversion support.
actual_capabilities: Creates single-file HTML presentations with inline CSS and JavaScript.
Guides style discovery through curated visual presets and preview slides.
Uses viewport rules to keep each slide within the visible browser area.
Converts PPTX content into extracted text, images, notes, and HTML slides.
Adds optional browser-based inline editing with localStorage saving.
Provides animation patterns for reveals, backgrounds, and interactive effects.
limitations: PPTX conversion requires Python and the python-pptx package.
Generated decks may need browser testing for exact layout and animation behavior.
Remote fonts can require network access unless replaced with local assets.
The skill is focused on HTML presentations, not native PowerPoint export.

use_cases.title: Create a Product Pitch Deck
use_cases.description: Turn product notes, screenshots, and a target tone into a browser-ready animated pitch deck.

use_cases.title: Convert a Training Presentation
use_cases.description: Extract content from a PPTX file and rebuild it as a responsive HTML lesson with clearer pacing.

use_cases.title: Improve an Existing HTML Deck
use_cases.description: Refine slide density, visual hierarchy, animations, and viewport fit in a current presentation.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Deck
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with topic and audience.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a short HTML slide deck about [topic] for [audience]. Use 6 slides, a professional style, and no inline editing.

prompt_templates.title: Design From Notes and Images
prompt_templates.prompt: Build an animated HTML presentation from these notes and images. Evaluate the images first, propose a slide outline, then create the final deck.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a PPTX File
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request that uses the extraction script.
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this PPTX into a responsive HTML presentation. Extract text, images, and speaker notes, then ask me to choose a visual style before generation.

prompt_templates.title: Upgrade an Existing Deck
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced refinement of current HTML output.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this HTML presentation for overflow, weak hierarchy, and generic design. Improve the deck while preserving content and browser navigation.

output_examples.input: A founder provides rough product launch notes and asks for a 10 slide investor deck.
output_examples.output: A self-contained HTML deck with a title slide, problem section, product story, traction slides, and a strong closing slide.

output_examples.input: A trainer uploads a PowerPoint course and wants a web version for workshops.
output_examples.output: Extracted slide content is reorganized into responsive lessons with speaker notes preserved as comments and images placed in assets.

output_examples.input: A developer shares an existing HTML deck that overflows on small screens.
output_examples.output: The deck is split into balanced slides, typography uses viewport-safe sizing, and navigation remains usable on desktop and mobile.

best_practices: Confirm audience, slide count, source content, and editing needs before generation.
Review generated previews before committing to a final visual direction.
Test the final HTML deck at desktop, tablet, and short-height viewport sizes.
anti_patterns: Do not cram long documents into a few dense slides.
Do not enable inline editing when the user only needs a static presentation.
Do not rely on remote fonts when the deck must work offline.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates self-contained HTML presentations with responsive layouts, animation, navigation, and optional inline editing.

faq.question: Can it convert PowerPoint files?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a Python extraction script for PPTX text, images, and notes before generating an HTML deck.

faq.question: Does it need a build tool?
faq.answer: No. The intended output is a single HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript.

faq.question: Can the presentation work offline?
faq.answer: Yes, if remote fonts and other external assets are replaced with local or embedded assets.

faq.question: Does it support direct text editing?
faq.answer: Yes. Inline editing is optional and should only be included when the user requests it.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
